name: Reycob WebP e Iconos
author: Victor Rodriguez

sections.description:
Reycob WebP and SVG Icons provides two independent tools for WordPress sites:

  • Converts new JPG and PNG uploads to WebP when the server supports WebP encoding.
  • Compresses WebP files with a configurable quality level from 50 to 95.
  • Scans existing JPG and PNG media attachments from an administrator-only screen.
  • Converts existing images and their registered thumbnail sizes in small AJAX batches.
  • Keeps previous files as compatibility backups when migrating existing media.
  • Validates file size, image type, and pixel dimensions before decoding a source image.
  • Prevents overlapping optimization batches from processing the same attachment concurrently.
  • Adds a local SVG icon catalog to the Elementor icon selector.
  • Renders compatible legacy icon markup as inline SVG with currentColor support.
  • Lets administrators enable or disable image conversion and the Elementor icon library independently.

All image processing happens on the site’s own server through the WordPress image editor or Imagick. The plugin does not use an external optimization service, transmit media files, add tracking, or load remote code.

When WebP encoding is unavailable or a new upload cannot be converted, the original JPG or PNG remains unchanged. Existing-library conversion only updates an attachment after the main file and its registered image sizes have been created successfully.

The Elementor integration is optional. Image conversion and the media scanner continue to work when Elementor is not installed.

Privacy

The plugin does not collect personal data, use cookies, track administrators or visitors, or send information to external services.

Image files are processed locally on the WordPress server. The scanner stores only plugin settings, a temporary list of attachment IDs that could not be converted, and migration metadata needed to manage compatibility files.

Third-Party Resources

The bundled Elementor icon names and SVG path data are adapted from the ElementsKit Lite icon pack by Wpmet, distributed under the GPLv3 or later license. See third-party-notices.txt for source, copyright, license, and modification details.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/reycob-webp-e-iconos/, or install it through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate Reycob WebP e Iconos.
  3. Go to Media > WebP e Iconos.
  4. Choose the WebP quality and enable the modules you want to use.
  5. Use Scan media library before starting an existing-media conversion.

Create a full site and uploads backup before processing a large existing media library.
sections.faq:
What happens if my server cannot create WebP files?

The plugin leaves new JPG and PNG uploads unchanged and shows the WebP engine as unavailable on its settings screen. The existing-media converter cannot start until WordPress detects WebP support through GD or Imagick.

Are original files deleted?

After a new upload is successfully converted and validated, its temporary JPG or PNG source is replaced by the WebP file before the attachment enters the Media Library.

When existing Media Library attachments are migrated, previous JPG and PNG files are kept at their original URLs as compatibility backups. WordPress attachment metadata is updated to use the new WebP files.

Does uninstalling restore converted images?

No. Uninstalling removes the plugin settings and temporary failure list, but it does not rewrite attachment metadata, restore image formats, or delete media files. This avoids destructive changes during plugin removal.

Does the plugin send images to an external service?

No. Image encoding is performed locally by the WordPress image editor or Imagick available on the hosting server.

Is Elementor required?

No. Elementor is only required to use the optional SVG icon catalog. The WebP features work independently.

Why are some old JPG or PNG files still on the server after a scan?

The scanner preserves the previous files as compatibility backups so older direct URLs do not break. They are removed when the corresponding migrated attachment is permanently deleted while the plugin is active.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • Added resource-safety checks before JPG and PNG files are opened by the image engine.
  • Added an atomic, self-expiring lock to prevent concurrent media conversion batches.
  • Added cleanup for the temporary scanner lock during uninstall.

1.0.0

  • Initial WordPress.org release.
  • Added safe WebP conversion for new JPG and PNG uploads.
  • Added batched conversion for existing Media Library attachments and registered thumbnail sizes.
  • Added configurable compression quality and independent module switches.
  • Added an optional local SVG icon library for Elementor.
  • Added local-only processing with no tracking or external connections.
